dictees.texte: My name is Tom and I am eleven years old. I live in a small house in Brighton with my parents and my sister, Emma. We have got a dog called Biscuit. He is brown and white and he loves playing in the garden.

dictees.texte: I get up at seven o’clock every morning. I have breakfast with my brother and then we walk to school. Lessons start at half past eight. My favourite subject is art because I love drawing. At lunchtime, I eat in the canteen with my friends.

dictees.texte: Last Saturday, my cousins came to visit us. In the morning, we went to the market and bought some fruit. In the afternoon, it was sunny, so we played football in the park. In the evening, Dad cooked pizza and we watched a funny film. It was a great day!

dictees.texte: Last summer, I visited London with my class. We saw Big Ben and the London Eye, and we took a boat on the Thames. The weather wasn’t very good: it rained every day! But I wasn’t disappointed, because the city was amazing. I bought a model of a red bus for my little brother.

dictees.texte: Next summer, my family and I are going to travel to Scotland. We are going to rent a small cottage near a lake. I hope the weather will be nice, but I will take a raincoat just in case! My dad wants to climb Ben Nevis, the highest mountain in the United Kingdom. I think it will be difficult, but I am sure we will enjoy the view.

dictees.texte: Thomas Edison was born in the United States in 1847. As a child, he was very curious and he asked a lot of questions. He didn’t stay at school for long, so his mother taught him at home. Later, he became one of the most famous inventors in history. He is often remembered for the light bulb, but he also invented the phonograph.

dictees.texte: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges of our time. Scientists say that we must reduce our greenhouse gas emissions as quickly as possible. Everyone can help: we can walk or cycle instead of taking the car, eat less meat and avoid wasting food. If we all make small changes, we will make a big difference. It isn’t too late, but we have to act now.

dictees.texte: On 1 December 1955, in Montgomery, Alabama, a Black woman called Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a bus to a white passenger. At that time, segregation laws separated Black and white people in many places. Rosa Parks was arrested, but her courage inspired a huge protest. For more than a year, Black people refused to use the city’s buses. In 1956, the Supreme Court ruled that segregation on buses was unconstitutional.
